title: Judges Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 19.

questions.question: Where was the Levite sojourning when he took a concubine?
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Ephraim
questions.explanation: The Levite was sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim when he took a concubine (Judges 19:1).

questions.question: How long did the concubine remain in her father's house in Bethlehemjudah?
questions.correctAnswer: Four whole months
questions.explanation: She was there four whole months in her father's house (Judges 19:2).

questions.question: What did the Levite bring with him when he went to speak to his concubine?
options: His servant and a couple of asses
questions.correctAnswer: His servant and a couple of asses
questions.explanation: He went after her having his servant with him and a couple of asses (Judges 19:3).

questions.question: How many days did the Levite stay at his father-in-law's house initially?
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: He abode with his father-in-law three days, eating, drinking, and lodging there (Judges 19:4).

questions.question: What did the father-in-law offer the Levite on the fourth day before he departed?
questions.correctAnswer: A morsel of bread
questions.explanation: On the fourth day, the father-in-law said, 'Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward go your way' (Judges 19:5).

questions.question: True or False: The father-in-law urged the Levite to stay all night on the fourth day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The father-in-law urged him to stay all night on the fourth day (Judges 19:6).

questions.question: Did the Levite immediately leave after the third day of lodging with his father-in-law?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: When the man rose to depart, his father-in-law urged him to stay again, so he lodged there again (Judges 19:7).

questions.question: On the fifth day, how long did the Levite and the father-in-law tarry before departing?
questions.correctAnswer: Until afternoon
questions.explanation: They tarried until afternoon on the fifth day before departing (Judges 19:8).

questions.question: What did the father-in-law say as the day drew toward evening on the fifth day?
options: Tarry all night and lodge here
questions.correctAnswer: Tarry all night and lodge here
questions.explanation: He urged them to tarry all night so their hearts might be merry and to leave early the next day (Judges 19:9).

questions.question: True or False: The Levite accepted his father-in-law's invitation and stayed the night.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The man would not tarry that night but rose up and departed (Judges 19:10).

questions.question: What city did the Levite and his company come near to when the day was far spent?
questions.correctAnswer: Jebus (Jerusalem)
questions.explanation: They came over against Jebus, which is Jerusalem, when the day was far spent (Judges 19:10-11).

questions.question: Why did the Levite refuse to lodge in Jebus?
options: Because it was a city of strangers, not of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was a city of strangers, not of Israel
questions.explanation: He said they would not turn into the city of a stranger, that is not of the children of Israel (Judges 19:12).

questions.question: Which two places did the Levite suggest as lodging options after refusing Jebus?
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeah and Ramah
questions.explanation: He suggested lodging all night in Gibeah or Ramah (Judges 19:13).

questions.question: In Judges 19, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread
Tarry all night and lodge here
Get you early on your way tomorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread
questions.explanation: The first instruction given on the fourth day was 'Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward go your way' (Judges 19:5), which comes before the other instructions.

questions.question: True or False: The Levite's concubine was with him when he departed from his father-in-law's house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The concubine was with him when he departed (Judges 19:10).

medium.title: Judges Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did the Levite and his group choose not to lodge in the city of Jebus (Jerusalem)?
options: Because it was a city of strangers and not of the children of Israel
Because the city was full and had no room for them
Because they feared the Jebusite army
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was a city of strangers and not of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 19:12 states the master would not turn into the city of a stranger, which was not of the children of Israel, showing a preference for lodging among fellow Israelites. This is supported by Judges 19:11 where the servant suggests lodging in Jebus, and Judges 19:13 where they decide on Gibeah or Ramah instead.

questions.question: What does the old man's invitation to lodge at his house teach us about hospitality?
options: Hospitality involves providing shelter and meeting the needs of travelers
Hospitality requires heavy feasting and celebration
Hospitality means inviting everyone in the city to a party
Hospitality is only for family members
questions.correctAnswer: Hospitality involves providing shelter and meeting the needs of travelers
questions.explanation: Judges 19:20-21 shows the old man warmly welcomes the wayfaring man, provides for the asses, and offers shelter to avoid lodging in the street. This exemplifies practical hospitality as caring for the needs of strangers.

questions.question: Based on Judges 19:15-16, what challenge did the Levite face when seeking lodging in Gibeah?
options: No one was willing to take them into their house for lodging
The city was in the middle of a war
There was a severe famine in the city
The city was closed to travelers
questions.correctAnswer: No one was willing to take them into their house for lodging
questions.explanation: Judges 19:15 explains the Levite sat in the street because no man took them into his house, showing a lack of hospitality from the city dwellers. Judges 19:16 introduces the old man who does offer lodging, highlighting this contrast.

questions.question: What can we learn about trust and discernment from the Levite’s decision to go to Gibeah instead of Jebus?
options: It shows prudent trust in God’s people and avoiding potentially unsafe places
It shows fear and lack of faith to avoid cities
It shows indifference to where they stayed
It shows disobedience to God’s instructions
questions.correctAnswer: It shows prudent trust in God’s people and avoiding potentially unsafe places
questions.explanation: Judges 19:12 reflects the Levite’s decision to avoid a city of strangers and stay among Israelites, demonstrating discernment about where to place trust. This aligns with practical Christian living where believers seek safe fellowship and community.

questions.question: How does Judges 19:18-19 highlight the importance of contentment and preparedness when traveling?
options: The Levite mentions they have straw, provender, bread, and wine, showing they came prepared and were content
They complained about having no food or drink
They demanded others to provide for them
They refused to travel without servants
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite mentions they have straw, provender, bread, and wine, showing they came prepared and were content
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 18 show the Levite acknowledging their provisions and lack of want, teaching contentment and readiness when on journeys. This helps believers understand the value of trusting God while being responsible.

questions.question: What is the significance of the old man telling the Levite 'only lodge not in the street' in Judges 19:20?
options: It emphasizes the need for safety and protection during the night
It means the street was closed for repairs
It implies the Levite was not welcome in the city
It suggests the old man wanted to keep his house private
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the need for safety and protection during the night
questions.explanation: The old man’s insistence in Judges 19:20 reflects concern for the Levite’s safety, highlighting the biblical virtue of protecting the vulnerable. Staying in a house offers security compared to the dangers of the street at night.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 19:13-14, the Levite and his servants considered lodging in both Gibeah and Ramah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 19:13 clearly states the man said to his servant to draw near to one of these places to lodge: Gibeah or Ramah, indicating they considered both options before choosing Gibeah.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Gibeah welcomed the Levite and his group warmly, offering them lodging immediately according to Judges 19.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 19:15 states no man took them into his house to lodge, forcing the Levite to sit in the street. This shows a lack of initial hospitality from the men of Gibeah.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is demonstrated by the old man from Mount Ephraim in Judges 19:16-21?
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity and kindness toward strangers
questions.explanation: The old man welcomes the Levite, provides for his animals, and offers food and lodging, demonstrating generosity and kindness as commanded in scripture (Judges 19:16-21).

questions.question: How does Judges 19:11-13 illustrate the importance of wise decision-making in daily life?
options: The Levite listens to his servant’s advice but ultimately makes a considered choice about where to lodge
They choose the first place suggested without thought
They ignore all advice and wander randomly
They stay in the city of Jebus as the servant requested
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite listens to his servant’s advice but ultimately makes a considered choice about where to lodge
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 show the servant suggests lodging in Jebus, but the Levite decides to pass over to Gibeah or Ramah, showing a process of advice and thoughtful decision-making, a practical application for believers.

questions.question: What does Judges 19:18 reveal about the Levite's attitude toward rejection and hospitality?
options: He acknowledges being rejected but continues his journey with humility and faith
He becomes angry and curses the city
He refuses to move on and stays in Bethlehemjudah
He retaliates against those who rejected him
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledges being rejected but continues his journey with humility and faith
questions.explanation: Judges 19:18 records the Levite explaining that no man receives him to house, yet he remains on his way to the house of the LORD, showing humility and perseverance despite rejection.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trust and provision can Christians learn from Judges 19:19-20 in the context of traveling or hardship?
options: Trust God for provision but bring what you can and accept help from others
Do not travel without a large entourage
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God for provision but bring what you can and accept help from others
questions.explanation: The Levite carries provisions (Judges 19:19) and the old man offers help (Judges 19:20), teaching believers to combine faith with practical preparedness and community support.

questions.question: True or False: The old man from Mount Ephraim was a native of Gibeah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 19:16 states the old man sojourned in Gibeah but was from mount Ephraim, indicating he was a resident but not a native of Gibeah.

questions.question: How does the interaction between the Levite and the old man in Judges 19:17-21 model Christian responses to strangers or those in need?
options: Engage with kindness, offer shelter, and provide for needs without hesitation
Avoid strangers and keep to oneself
questions.correctAnswer: Engage with kindness, offer shelter, and provide for needs without hesitation
questions.explanation: The old man greets the Levite, inquires about his journey, and offers lodging and provisions (Judges 19:17-21), demonstrating the biblical call to hospitality and compassion.

questions.question: What does Judges 19:14 teach us about timing and decision-making?
options: The sun setting indicates urgency to find lodging before night falls
They had plenty of time and chose to rest
The sun rising caused them to delay
They ignored the time and continued traveling all night
questions.correctAnswer: The sun setting indicates urgency to find lodging before night falls
questions.explanation: Judges 19:14 notes the sun went down upon them by Gibeah, emphasizing the practical need to find lodging promptly, teaching believers to be mindful of timing in decisions.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 19.

questions.question: What did the old man offer to the Levite and his party when they arrived in Gibeah?
options: A place to lodge and food for their asses
Silver and gold as a gift
A guide to the next city
questions.correctAnswer: A place to lodge and food for their asses
questions.explanation: The old man brought them into his house, gave provender to the asses, and they washed their feet and ate and drank (Judges 19:21).

questions.question: What term is used in Judges 19:22 to describe the men who beset the house and demanded the Levite be brought out?
questions.correctAnswer: Sons of Belial
questions.explanation: The text explicitly calls the men 'sons of Belial' who beset the house and beat at the door (Judges 19:22). The term 'Belial' indicates wickedness or worthlessness.

questions.question: How did the master of the house try to prevent the men from doing harm to the Levite?
options: He offered his daughter and the Levite's concubine instead
He hid the Levite in a secret room
He pleaded with the men to leave peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: He offered his daughter and the Levite's concubine instead
questions.explanation: The master of the house said, 'Behold, here is my daughter a maiden, and his concubine; them I will bring out now... but unto this man do not so vile a thing' (Judges 19:24).

questions.question: What tragic event happened to the Levite's concubine during the night in Gibeah?
options: She was abused by the men of the city
She escaped and fled to Bethlehem
She was taken captive by another tribe
She was protected by the old man
questions.correctAnswer: She was abused by the men of the city
questions.explanation: The men abused her all night until morning, as stated in Judges 19:25.

questions.question: Where did the concubine go at the break of dawn after being abused?
options: She fell down at the door of the man's house
She fled to the city square
She hid in the fields outside the city
She returned to her father's house
questions.correctAnswer: She fell down at the door of the man's house
questions.explanation: At dawn, she came and fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was, as described in Judges 19:26.

questions.question: What did the Levite do when he found his concubine at the door in the morning?
options: He took her up on an ass and went home
He carried her inside and prayed
He sought help from the old man
He left her and fled the city
questions.correctAnswer: He took her up on an ass and went home
questions.explanation: He took her up upon an ass and went to his place (Judges 19:28).

questions.question: What horrific action did the Levite take upon returning home with his concubine?
options: He divided her body into twelve pieces and sent them throughout Israel
He sought justice from the elders
He left her body at the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: He divided her body into twelve pieces and sent them throughout Israel
questions.explanation: He took a knife and divided her into twelve pieces, sending them to all the coasts of Israel (Judges 19:29).

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people who saw the Levite’s act of dividing the concubine's body?
options: They said no such deed was done or seen since Israel came out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They said no such deed was done or seen since Israel came out of Egypt
questions.explanation: All that saw it said there was no such deed done or seen since Israel came out of Egypt (Judges 19:30).

questions.question: Which city did the Levite refuse to lodge in because it was a city of strangers, not of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jebus (Jerusalem)
questions.explanation: He refused to turn into the city of Jebus, which was not of the children of Israel (Judges 19:12).

questions.question: True or False: The Levite's concubine played the harlot against him and left to her father's house for four months.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The concubine played the whore against him and went to her father's house for four months (Judges 19:2).

questions.question: True or False: The old man in Gibeah was a Benjamite by birth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The old man was from mount Ephraim but sojourned in Gibeah; the men of the place were Benjamites (Judges 19:16).

questions.question: Which other biblical event echoes the theme of hospitality turned into violence found in Judges 19?
options: Lot and the men of Sodom in Genesis 19
Moses and the burning bush in Exodus 3
Noah and the flood in Genesis 6
questions.correctAnswer: Lot and the men of Sodom in Genesis 19
questions.explanation: Genesis 19 describes how Lot offered hospitality in Sodom but faced violent demands from men of the city, paralleling the abuse and wickedness in Judges 19 (Judges 19:22-25; Genesis 19).

questions.question: What is the significance of the Levite sending twelve pieces of his concubine’s body throughout Israel?
options: To summon all the tribes of Israel to respond to the atrocity
To distribute her remains according to tribal custom
questions.correctAnswer: To summon all the tribes of Israel to respond to the atrocity
questions.explanation: Sending twelve pieces symbolically called all twelve tribes to take counsel and act against the crime (Judges 19:29-30).

questions.question: From a Hebrew word study, what does the term 'sons of Belial' imply about the men who beset the house?
options: They are worthless and wicked men
questions.correctAnswer: They are worthless and wicked men
questions.explanation: 'Belial' in Hebrew denotes worthlessness or wickedness, indicating these men were morally corrupt (Judges 19:22).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the structure of Judges 19, especially in the framing of hospitality and violence?
options: Inclusio — framing the narrative with hospitality and its perversion
Simile — comparing the concubine to a dove
Metaphor — the city as a lion
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio — framing the narrative with hospitality and its perversion
questions.explanation: The chapter is framed by acts of hospitality that are perverted into violence, creating an inclusio that highlights the moral decay (Judges 19:21 and 19:22-25).

theological.title: Judges Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the initial situation described in Judges 19:1 reveal about the governance of Israel during this period?
options: There was a king ruling Israel with full authority
Israel was governed by judges without a central king
The Levite was the king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was governed by judges without a central king
questions.explanation: Judges 19:1 states 'when there was no king in Israel', indicating Israel was under a decentralized tribal system governed by judges rather than a monarchic rule, highlighting a period of social and political instability.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the Levite's concubine's departure and the husband's attempt to reconcile as seen in Judges 19:2-3?
options: Doctrine of human sin and relational brokenness
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of human sin and relational brokenness
questions.explanation: Judges 19:2-3 show a broken human relationship where the concubine commits unfaithfulness and departs, and the husband seeks reconciliation, illustrating the pervasive effects of sin on human relationships and the need for restoration.

questions.question: How does Judges 19:4-7 reveal the cultural and social obligations of hospitality in ancient Israel?
options: Hospitality was optional and rarely practiced
Hospitality was a sacred duty involving provision and protection
Hospitality was only for family members
Hospitality was forbidden on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Hospitality was a sacred duty involving provision and protection
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 describe the father-in-law hosting the Levite for multiple days with food and drink, urging him to stay longer, reflecting the cultural imperative of hospitality as a moral and social obligation to strangers and family alike.

questions.question: What divine attribute is indirectly challenged by the violent events in Judges 19:22-25?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and justice
questions.explanation: The brutal abuse of the concubine in verses 22-25 represents a deep violation of God's holy standards and justice, highlighting human sinfulness and the need for divine judgment to uphold righteousness.

questions.question: What does the Levite's action of dividing his concubine's body into twelve pieces in Judges 19:29 demonstrate about the social and religious condition of Israel at the time?
options: Israel was experiencing profound moral decay and tribal disunity
Israel was under strict Mosaic Law enforcement
Israel was preparing for the monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was experiencing profound moral decay and tribal disunity
questions.explanation: Judges 19:29 shows a shocking act meant to shock all tribes of Israel, symbolizing the grave social disintegration and moral chaos without central leadership, as also reflected in the chapter's opening context.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Judges 19:15-21 illustrate the theme of alienation and the lack of genuine community in Israel?
options: The Levite was warmly received by many hosts
The Levite and his group were rejected by all but one old man, showing social alienation
The Levite was welcomed as a king
The city of Gibeah was known for its hospitality
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite and his group were rejected by all but one old man, showing social alienation
questions.explanation: Verses 15-21 describe the Levite's difficulty finding lodging and only one old man offering hospitality, indicating social alienation and fractured community bonds in Israel at the time.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Judges 19:5-6 and Judges 19:11-14 provide about divine providence and human agency?
options: God completely controls all human actions without human responsibility
Human beings have free will, but God’s providence allows encounters that reveal societal sin
God is absent from human decisions
Human agency is irrelevant due to predestination
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings have free will, but God’s providence allows encounters that reveal societal sin
questions.explanation: In verses 5-6 and 11-14, the Levite is urged to stay or not stay, and his decisions lead them to Gibeah, where the tragic events unfold; this shows human responsibility within God's overarching providential plan to expose Israel's sin.

questions.question: What doctrine is reflected in Judges 19:30 when the people respond to the Levite’s gruesome act by saying no such deed has been seen since the Exodus?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of covenant accountability
questions.explanation: Judges 19:30 highlights Israel's recognition of a covenant-breaking sin so severe that it surpasses previous transgressions since the Exodus, emphasizing their corporate responsibility under God’s covenant.

questions.question: How does Judges 19:19-20 reflect the biblical principle of provision and refuge for the needy within the community?
options: Provision and shelter were duties of the community to travelers
Refuge was available only in religious festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Provision and shelter were duties of the community to travelers
questions.explanation: The old man in verses 19-20 invites the Levite to lodge in his house and provides for their needs, illustrating the biblical ethic of hospitality and care for strangers as part of social holiness.

questions.question: What attribute of God is underscored by the persistent presence of evil men in Judges 19:22 despite the cultural expectation of hospitality?
options: God's immediate judgment on all sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over evil
questions.explanation: Judges 19:22 shows evil men acting wickedly within Israel, demonstrating that while evil exists, God's sovereignty allows such events for judgment and eventual redemption (cf. Romans 8:28).

questions.question: What narrative arc does Judges 19:10-14 contribute to Israel’s historical trajectory in the Old Testament?
options: The moral decline leading to Israel’s need for a king
The building of the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The moral decline leading to Israel’s need for a king
questions.explanation: The Levite’s refusal to stay in Jebus and decision to go to Gibeah (Judges 19:10-14) situate the narrative in a context of moral and social decline, underscoring why Israel eventually demanded a monarchy for order.

questions.question: What synthesis theological lesson emerges from Judges 19:26-28 about human desensitization to sin and its consequences?
options: Sin always leads to immediate repentance
Desensitization to sin leads to tragic normalization of evil acts
questions.correctAnswer: Desensitization to sin leads to tragic normalization of evil acts
questions.explanation: The concubine’s silent, lifeless presence at the door (19:26-28) and the husband’s cold action reveal how normalized atrocity had become, illustrating the tragic spiritual deadness resulting from unchecked sin.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the Bible condones violence and injustice through stories like Judges 19:22-25. What does Judges 19:22-30 actually teach about God's stance on such acts?
options: It condemns violence and highlights the need for justice and repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It condemns violence and highlights the need for justice and repentance
questions.explanation: Judges 19:22-30 portrays the horrific violence as a symptom of Israel’s moral collapse, ending with a call for counsel and reflection, emphasizing condemnation of sin and the necessity of justice, not approval of violence.

questions.question: What combined teaching about human responsibility and divine judgment is evident from Judges 19:23-25 and Judges 19:29-30?
options: Human sin provokes divine judgment and communal accountability
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin provokes divine judgment and communal accountability
questions.explanation: The man’s offering of his daughter and concubine (19:23-25) and the Levite’s dismemberment and sending of her parts (19:29-30) show human sin leading to grave judgment and a call for Israel’s collective repentance and responsibility.

questions.question: How does Judges 19:17-18 highlight the theological tension between hospitality and the reality of sin in fallen human society?
options: It shows perfect hospitality without any sin
It contrasts the ideal of hospitality with the danger of encountering wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts the ideal of hospitality with the danger of encountering wickedness
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 show the old man welcoming a stranger with hospitality in contrast to the later menace from the city’s wicked men, illustrating the tension between God’s call for love and the reality of sin in society.
